strengths: Addresses important gap in evaluating cultural representation in T2I models through social activities rather than objects, with clear motivation
Substantial benchmark contribution (576 prompts, 16 countries, 19,000+ images) with systematic coverage of Global North and South
Novel AHEaD evaluation framework with interpretable descriptor-based metrics that demonstrate 7% better correlation with human judgments than VLM-based approaches
Rigorous human evaluation with proper quality controls (domain expertise verification, attention checks, consistency testing) confirming metric validity
Clear finding of systematic Global North bias across all tested T2I models (4-8% performance gaps) with detailed dimensional analysis
Addresses genuine limitation of existing metrics: showing that image-text alignment correlates positively with exaggeration while humans expect negative correlation
Comprehensive reproducibility support including detailed methodology, prompts in appendix, ablation studies, and threshold calibration explanation
weaknesses: Framework relies on LLM-generated descriptors which inherit Western-centric biases; while descriptor accuracy validated at 90.27% average, impact on final metrics across regions not analyzed
Human evaluation limited to 7 of 16 countries (44%) and 3 of 6 models (50%) with moderate human-human agreement (0.42-0.46), limiting confidence in generalization claims
Exaggeration metric design underspecified: selection of exaggeration candidates Sr is unclear, and metric fundamentally depends on noisy real image baselines subject to CLIPScore filtering bias
Threshold calibration (τ=0.52, 75th percentile) appears arbitrary; calibration on biased real images limits robustness; different thresholds may systematically favor different regions
Hallucination metric may incorrectly penalize valid cultural alternatives not in LLM-generated descriptors; limited validation that metric aligns with human hallucination understanding
Activity selection sourced from English-heavy CulturalAtlas and Wikipedia without analysis of representativeness across Global South countries
Real image collection methodology appears limited (20 candidates per prompt → 5 selected via CLIPScore), insufficient to capture activity variation across 16 countries
Statistical rigor lacking: no confidence intervals, significance tests, or p-values reported; 4-8% GN-GS gap claimed important without formal significance testing
Inconsistent metric behavior across perspectives: Figure 7 shows ALIGN/EXAG correlate differently with human scores than with model metrics, questioning what combined FAITH metric measures
Missing comparisons with concurrent work (CuRe, Nayak et al. 2025) beyond citations; limited exploration of sensitivity to proposer LLM choice (only GPT-4o and Gemini tested)

strengths: Addresses important underexplored problem: cultural faithfulness evaluation through social activities, moving beyond object-centric benchmarks
Comprehensive benchmark contribution: CULTIVate with 19,000+ images, 576 activities, 16 countries spanning Global North/South
Well-designed multi-dimensional evaluation framework: Alignment, Hallucination, Exaggeration, Diversity metrics are complementary and interpretable
Strong empirical results: FAITH achieves 27% higher correlation with human judgment (0.47) vs. MLLM baselines (0.20); demonstrates ITA metrics correlate poorly with human judgment
Thorough validation: 798 human annotations across 11 countries with detailed ablations (Tables 3-5) justify all metric components
Important finding: systematic 4-8% performance gap between Global North and Global South across all models, revealing systematic bias
Interpretable feedback: descriptor-level output enables diagnosis of specific failures and enables image editing applications
Strong reproducibility: extensive implementation details, prompts in appendix, descriptor validation (90% precision)
weaknesses: Fundamental limitation: Reference descriptors generated by LLMs which encode Western biases; using LLM-generated descriptors to evaluate T2I models creates potential circular bias that is acknowledged but not deeply addressed

Moderate inter-rater agreement (Krippendorff's Alpha 0.15-0.62, mean 0.33) reveals high subjectivity in cultural evaluation; human-human agreement (0.55) only marginally better than FAITH (0.47), limiting room for improvement
Contradictory use of ITA metrics: Paper criticizes ITA metrics' unreliability for cultural evaluation but uses VQAScore-based ITA in EXAG metric definition (Eq. 4), undermining this criticism

Threshold calibration lacks theoretical justification: τ selected at 75th percentile based on real images that themselves have biases; different thresholds needed for different MLLMs (0.52 vs 0.67) suggests fragility

Descriptor precision/recall incompletely validated: 90% precision reported but recall estimated indirectly through ratings (4.5/5) and missing descriptor counts (26/378) rather than direct measurement

Limited evaluation scope: Only 11 of 16 countries in human evaluation; 1-2 activities per category; 398 forms with 796 annotations is relatively small; proprietary T2I models evaluated with only 1 image each
Modest inter-rater agreement combined with direct real image filtering via CLIPScore (which paper critiques) creates methodological circularity in calibration
FAITH metric uses simple arithmetic mean of ALIGN, HAL, EXAG without justified weighting or ablation on aggregation method
Missing error analysis: Limited investigation of when/why FAITH diverges from human judgment; no analysis of why Global North models systematically outperform Global South
Limited generalization: Fixed prompt template ('A photorealistic photo...'); unclear if findings generalize to other prompt styles; only 6 T2I models tested
Descriptor-guided editing demonstration is preliminary (Fig. 8) without quantitative evaluation or analysis of scaling and prompt sensitivity
